endorsements.quote: For clinical integration to be successful, healthcare providers must be trained to interpret AI outputs.

Global health initiatives must prioritize investment in maternal health technologies and adopt a phased implementation strategy, starting in tertiary hospitals and supported by local validation studies, to facilitate equitable access to AI-based PE prediction tools.

Policymakers should prioritize funding for integrating these AI models into routine prenatal care, allocating resources for technology, provider training, and continuous validation to ensure quality care and health equity for all pregnant women.

unlisted_practices: Ensure ethical supervision so AI tools remain transparent, objective, and complementary to clinical judgment rather than a replacement for it.
Standardize biomarker assays across diverse populations and assays and maintain consistent outcome measures and thorough outcome ascertainment.
Conduct regular audits of biomarker measurement results and ensure personnel measuring biomarkers are properly trained.
Expand databases and validate AI performance in diverse populations.
Governments and international donors should collaborate on public-private partnerships to support biomarker testing and data-driven maternal care.

screen.reason: This is a letter/commentary discussing the potential, implementation considerations, and policy recommendations for AI-driven placental biomarker models for preeclampsia prediction.
